qt: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

On Friday 28 August, a Turkish drone embarked on a flight over the Thracian Sea lasting several hours. It flew in the wider area of Alexandroupoli and Samothrace and very close to Alexandroupoli airport. This dangerous violation by a Turkish drone marks yet another incident confirming the increase in Turkish provocations in the Aegean. It is telling that there were more than 247 instances of Turkish aircraft violating Greek airspace up to and including July this year compared to 225 during the whole of 2025. In fact, on 18 August, Turkish aircraft violated Greek national airspace 25 times, with Greek and Turkish F-16 armed fighter jets getting involved. In view of the ever-increasing violations of Greek airspace by Turkish fighter jets and drones, can the Commission say: 1.
What measures will it take, including potential sanctions against Türkiye, to protect Greek sovereign rights from Turkish provocation?

Does the Commission intend to propose the creation of a Southern Border Watch similar to the one foreseen for the eastern border, which would also include airspace violations, or to extend the implementation of the Eastern Flank Watch to Greece?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.10.2026) The EU is closely following developments in the Aegean Sea and remains attentive to actions liable to increase tensions in the region. The EU has repeatedly called on Türkiye to respect the sovereignty and sovereign rights of all Member States, and to commit itself unequivocally to good neighbourly relations, international agreements and the peaceful settlement of disputes. The Commission is continuously assessing Türkiye’s record regarding the respect of good neighbourly relations and will publish its conclusions in the upcoming Enlargement Package. The EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and remains committed to protecting its interests and those of its Member States, as well as to upholding regional stability. As regards border surveillance and airspace monitoring, the protection of the EU’s external borders is a shared responsibility between the EU and the Member States. Existing instruments, including support provided through the relevant EU agencies and operational frameworks, already contribute to situational awareness and border management at the EU’s external borders. Furthermore, the Commission stands ready to support Member State efforts through the European Defence Industry Programme1, including the European Defence Projects of Common Interest2. In this context, the Eastern Flank Watch and the DronE and Counter-Drone European Resolve (DECODER) can enhance the security and resilience of the entire EU territory and strengthen the EU’s defence readiness.
